## [0.45.0] - 2026-10-22

Read before updating: this version upgrades the workspace database in a way
earlier versions refuse, changes which files a request may send from disk, and
makes a collection run carry on after a script error or a failed connection.
Vayu now sends a request-body file only when you picked it in Vayu on this
machine or it lies under a folder allowed in Settings > Files, and nothing else
can claim a file was chosen. New: the real `uuid`, `lodash`, `moment`,
`csv-parse` and `xml2js` libraries in scripts, Postman's legacy script globals,
and History charts that open quickly on a 24-hour run.

### Added

- **`require()` runs the libraries Postman scripts use.** `require('uuid')`,
  `require('lodash')` with the `_` global, `require('moment')`,
  `require('csv-parse/lib/sync')` and `require('xml2js')` with `xml2Json` run
  the real npm libraries (#2650, #2651, #2652, #2653, #2654).
  `require('crypto-js')` and the `CryptoJS` global cover the MD5, SHA-1 and
  SHA-2 hashes, their HMACs and the Hex, Latin1, Utf8 and Base64 encoders
  (#2578). Any other module, and any other `CryptoJS` member such as AES, still
  throws and is named in the import notice.
- **Postman's legacy script API runs** (#2577): `tests[...]`, `postman.*`,
  `responseBody`, `setTimeout` and the other timers, and `await` at the top of
  a script. These scripts used to throw at their first line.
- **`pm.environment`, `pm.globals` and `pm.collectionVariables` accept a third
  argument to `set`** (#2664). `set(name, value, { secret: true })` creates a
  secret variable, and a type string (`'string'`, `'number'`, `'boolean'`,
  `'json'`) sets the type. A secret is masked from the next run on, not inside
  the run that created it.
- `pm.variables.set`, `unset` and `clear` write a run-local scope that is never
  stored (#2564). `pm.request.url.addQueryParams` and `removeQueryParams` work
  (#2662).
- **Import tells you what will not run.** The preview names the Postman
  requests whose scripts use APIs Vayu does not run (#2576), and the notice
  follows `CryptoJS` members reached through an alias or a destructure (#2628).
  It also names the GET body Postman never sends, and the Data file picker has
  **Read numbers as numbers** to match Newman's CSV reading (#2540). The
  "file changed since this run" hint also notices a different number reading
  (#2644).
- A Postman OAuth 2.0 collection keeps its `audience`, `resource` and other
  token request parameters (#2536). The OAuth 2.0 token and refresh tables
  choose per row whether it goes in the body, the query or a header (#2571).
- **MCP agents can follow and steer a run.** `get_run` reads a run's state, and
  a running run's report is marked partial (#2436). `run_request` sends a saved
  request by id when `url` is omitted (#2435). `start_load_run` states the
  shape it runs (#2437) and sets which response samples `get_run_samples`
  reads (#2447).

### Changed

- **The workspace database moves to schema version 7** (#2356, #2535). Once
  0.45.0 opens a workspace, earlier versions refuse it, so going back to 0.44
  means restoring a backup. The upgrade writes a copy of the database beside
  it first.
- **Data Safety Mode now defaults to Normal** (#2419). The workspace database
  used to run with Off, which can lose recent writes or corrupt the database
  on a power cut or a crash. Installs that never changed the setting move to
  Normal once, when 0.45.0 first opens the workspace; Settings > Data Safety
  Mode sets it back to Off.
- **A collection's folders and requests are numbered in one order** (#2535).
  The upgrade renumbers each collection's requests to follow its folders,
  including folders in the trash, so every collection lists and runs exactly
  as it did before. Like the rest of this upgrade it is one-way: an earlier
  engine refuses the workspace afterwards. A new folder or request, or one
  moved into a collection without a position, now goes after everything
  already in it, folders and requests alike. A Postman collection imports in
  the order Postman runs it: a request listed before or between folders stays
  there in the sidebar, the import preview and a run, instead of every folder
  moving above every request. A JMeter test plan and an Insomnia export (v4
  or v5) do the same (#2573): a plan's samplers and controllers import in the
  order the plan lists them, and an Insomnia folder's requests and sub-folders
  in the order Insomnia sorts them. Exporting to Postman or to OpenAPI writes that order back, so a round trip keeps it.
  For API clients, `POST /reorder` renumbers a parent's folders and requests
  together: a `normalize` entry is `{"parentId": <collection id or null>}`, and
  the old `{"type", "parentId"}` / `{"type", "collectionId"}` entries are refused with
  a 400.
- **A file is sent only once it is picked on this machine or sits under an
  allowed folder** (#2356). Files you chose before updating are carried over if
  they still exist. A file on a drive or network share that is not connected
  when 0.45.0 first opens the workspace is not carried over, even once the
  drive is back; the engine log names each one. A request naming any other
  file outside an allowed folder, or one of those, says *Not chosen on this
  machine* and is refused at Send until you pick the file again (Relink) or
  allow its folder.
- **Typing a path no longer counts as choosing the file.** A path typed into a
  binary body is sent only after you pick the file or allow its folder; the
  editor says so as you type.
- **Settings > Files adds folders through the folder picker only.** The field
  for typing a folder path is gone, and the import preview's Allow folder
  opens the picker at the folder it suggests.
- **An engine already running when the app starts is replaced.** The app no
  longer adopts one it did not start this session, including one started by
  hand in development; it is shut down and a new one started on the same port.
- **Allowing or removing a folder, and recording a picked file, need the app's
  grant secret.** The app passes its engine a fresh secret in
  `VAYU_GRANT_SECRET` at every start. Without it, `POST` and `DELETE` on
  `/file-roots` and `/file-grants` answer `403`, so an engine run by hand, by
  the CLI or in CI cannot change which files are sent; folders and files
  already allowed still apply.
- **`unresolved` in a request body is ignored.** The engine works out whether a
  file may be sent and reports it as `unresolved` when it returns a request; a
  value sent by a script, an MCP agent or an older client is dropped.
- **`[*]` and `..name` in a JSON extractor, assertion or metric follow the
  response's own member order** (#2459), where they used to sort by key. A
  `matchNo` of `1` now picks the member the server wrote first, and `-1`
  numbers the matches in that order.
- **A URL is sent as Postman sends it** (#2465). Send, load and collection
  runs, MCP and `pm.sendRequest` now put out the same request line for the
  same URL: `"`, `<` and `>` are percent-encoded in the path, query and
  fragment, a backtick in the path and fragment, `{` and `}` in the path, and
  `'` in the query. A backslash before the query becomes `/`, and the host is
  lowercased and a non-ASCII one sent by its punycode name. An escape already
  in the URL and every other byte go out unchanged, so a pre-signed URL still
  matches its signature. To send a URL exactly as typed, turn on Send URL
  without encoding for that request.

- **A script error or a failed connection no longer ends a collection run's
  iteration** (#2526). The step is reported as errored and the run moves on to
  the next request, as Postman and Newman do. Before, every step after the
  error in that iteration was skipped. The Run Collection dialog has a **Stop
  the iteration on a script error** switch, off by default, that restores the
  old behaviour for every kind of error; with it on, the run header says how
  many steps did not run. The error rate and any threshold on it now count the
  steps that used to be skipped. API clients send `stopOnError`.
- **Run history keeps design Sends under their own cap** (#2429). 200 quick
  Sends used to push last week's load and collection runs out of History. Those
  keep `maxRunsRetained` (200); Sends have `maxDesignRunsRetained` (100, 0 for
  no limit). **Clear run history now keeps pinned runs**, and runs still in
  progress, and the dialog says how many it keeps.
- **Timeouts and requests with no response count in the latency figures**
  (#2384, #2412). A load run where 5% of requests timed out used to report a
  fast p99 and could pass a latency budget. A timed-out request is stored with
  the time it waited rather than 0 ms, and a URL refused before connecting is
  not counted as a timed sample.
- **A text body is sent as `text/plain`, and a POST with no body sends no
  Content-Type** (#2464). Both used to go out as
  `application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, which a server that parses by type read
  as form fields.
- **Every enabled header row is sent, in the order typed** (#2466). Three
  `X-Dup` rows used to collapse into one, and repeated headers such as `Link`
  or two `Cookie` rows could not be sent. Header names and credentials are
  trimmed, and a name that is not a valid header name is refused (#2467).
- Large uploads no longer carry `Expect: 100-continue` unless `sendExpectContinue` is on
  (#2468). It added up to a second to
  every transfer over 1 MiB, and load-run comparisons now flag two runs that
  differ in it (#2516).
- A credential set by a pre-request script reaches the wire (#2473). A Basic
  auth password set there used to go out as the literal `{{password}}`. Auth
  is now applied after the script, as in Postman.
- A pm scope `set` ticks the row it writes (#2479), and a value a script sets
  keeps its type for the run (#2529, #2568). `pm.environment.set('n', get('n')
  + 1)` used to give `"01"`, and an object set on a json variable stored
  `[object Object]`.
- **`pm.expect` and `pm.response` assertions follow Postman and chai** (#2523,
  #2524, #2528, #2581, #2582). `.to.be.true` needs a real boolean (below),
  `.to.have.property(name)` moves the chain to the property's value, and
  `jsonSchema` checks `email`, `uri`, `uuid`, `hostname` and `ipv6` formats.
  A test that leaned on the old verdict can now fail.
- Storage failures answer `507`, `503` or `500`, not `400` (#2423, #2319,
  #2353). The app treated a `400` as final and stopped retrying the save;
  the quit prompt now says when the disk is full (#2685).
- The Auth tab says an API key sent in a header follows a redirect to another
  host, as Bearer and Basic do not (#2476). Imported Digest, AWS, NTLM, Hawk,
  OAuth 1, EdgeGrid and JWT auth show as not sent (#2474, #2537, #2610), and
  MCP refuses an unknown auth mode instead of sending with none (#2477).
- Internal work is folded here: CI and release pipeline changes, test
  stability, the clang-tidy push hook, README and comparison-page claims, and
  an upgrade of the bundled JavaScript engine.

### Fixed

- The response pane's Pretty view, Copy, Download, Save as example and the Raw
  tab show a JSON body as the server sent it (#2459). They showed a copy with
  its keys sorted, repeated keys merged and integers past 2^53 rounded, and a
  mock server answered with that copy. A streamed response's event payloads
  are shown as sent too.

- **A redirect loop and an undecodable response are no longer reported as
  "Couldn't connect"** (#2462). A send that exceeds Maximum redirects now fails
  with `TOO_MANY_REDIRECTS`, and a response whose `Content-Encoding` its bytes
  are not in, or that Vayu cannot decode, fails with `BAD_CONTENT_ENCODING`;
  each message says which limit or encoding was involved. A script that tested
  `err.code` in `pm.sendRequest`, or `pm.response.errorCode`, against
  `'CONNECTION_FAILED'` for these cases now sees the new spelling. A load run
  records them as `too_many_redirects` and `bad_content_encoding`.
- **The raw request after a 301, 302 or 303 no longer shows a body the final
  request never sent** (#2462). A POST answered by one of these is re-sent as a
  GET without its body, and the raw request now ends at the headers to match.
  307 and 308 keep the body, and so does the view.
- **A failure inside an `async` test or a promise is reported** (#2531). A
  script's `.then` callbacks and the code after an `await` now run as part of
  the script, within its time limit, and a rejected promise
  nothing handles fails the step with *Unhandled promise rejection*, naming
  the test when it came from `pm.test("name", async () => ...)`. The test row
  itself stays passed, as Postman records it. These scripts used to pass with
  their assertions never counted.

- **`pm.expect(x).to.be.true` and `.to.be.false` now require a real boolean**
  (#2523), as in Postman. They passed for any truthy or falsy value, so
  `pm.expect(1).to.be.true` and `pm.expect('').to.be.false` were green. An
  imported test that leaned on that now fails, with a message that names the
  value ("Expected 1 to be true"). Use `.to.be.ok` for a truthiness check.

- **A response that is not valid UTF-8 is shown** (#2458). An image, a PDF, a
  Latin-1 page or an undecoded gzip body made Send fail with an empty `500`
  although the server answered 200.
- **Latency and rate charts match what the run did** (#2385, #2386, #2393,
  #2589, #2611). A stored or live tick held the percentiles of only the last
  tenth of its second, so a stall inside a second vanished. The Throughput over
  time, Send rate and Latency mean charts plotted run-so-far averages (a 2 s
  outage in a 20 s run looked like a 15 percent dip), and a second with no
  completions drew 0 ms in the run's worst second. They now cover the trailing
  second. Live anomaly marks match History's, and a long run's server vitals
  load as at most 2000 points.
- A long run opens fast in History (#2547): the page reads at most 2000 folded
  points instead of paging in every second of a 24-hour run.
- Rate fidelity and send rate divide by the sending window, not the drain
  (#2392), and the live clock starts when load starts, as the report's does
  (#2395). The Slow requests card counts every slow completion, not the stored
  sample (#2399). A capacity level is judged on its own p99, not the mean of
  its windows (#2388). A transaction sums its members in microseconds, so fast
  members no longer count as 0 ms (#2387).
- The status chart's first bar is a rate over its own interval when the live
  window starts late (#2401). Chart marker and annotation labels no longer
  print over each other (#2696), the History charts have the dashboard's
  legends (#2697), and the breakpoint line names the SLO and draws it on the
  percentile chart (#2698).
- A re-authorized OAuth 2.0 config exchanges the new code instead of returning
  the cached token (#2472), and a stray request to the loopback callback no
  longer fails a pending sign-in (#2369).
- The Cookies tab shows a `Set-Cookie` sent on a redirect hop (#2461), and
  response headers are shown as received, repeated `Set-Cookie` lines included
  (#2460). A proxy on `https://` is verified with the same CA bundle and
  Verify TLS setting as the target (#2469). A space in the URL or a path
  variable is encoded instead of failing as a bad scheme (#2465).
- A snippet sends one `Authorization` header, as the engine does (#2475), and
  masks a secret in the URL host (#2591). The Code section and the tab title
  follow the editor's unsaved state and resolved URL (#2637, #2638), and the
  Send-with-row preview escapes a cell as the send does (#2639).
- A data-driven run binds `{{data.col}}` in a form-data text part's type
  (#2572).
- **Postman imports keep more of the collection.** A folder's or collection's
  `protocolProfileBehavior` (redirects, TLS) applies to its requests (#2538).
  A raw `html` or `javascript` body keeps its Content-Type, and a form-data
  text part keeps its own (#2539). A string-form `header`, a URL `#fragment`
  and a script loaded from a URL are kept or counted (#2541). `pm.sendRequest`
  sends urlencoded and form-data bodies (#2563).
- An OpenAPI export keeps who saved each example, so a re-import does not
  replace one you saved (#2430).
- Several freezes are gone: expanding a 1,000-request folder (#2543), opening
  the command palette with thousands of requests (#2545), launching a large
  workspace (#2546), polling History and a live run's report (#2548, #2659,
  #2679), and a 100,000-key JSON body taking minutes to parse or export (#2497,
  #2552). A 20 MB response no longer leaves the engine 200 MB larger (#2544).
- A locked or full database at startup is refused, not moved aside as corrupt
  (#2420), and the recovery backup is refreshed and flushed at shutdown (#2421).
  Deleting `vayu.lock` no longer lets a second engine start (#2422), and a
  failed migration commit no longer reads as a finished migration (#2425).
- When Vayu's engine does not answer or will not restart, the message names
  the failure and a next step (#2292, #2297). Settings shows why the MCP server
  is not listening and stops offering its endpoint (#2368), and a failed inbox
  start or import fetch reads as one message (#2295).
- Accessibility and wording sweep: unnamed controls in the variables table,
  delete dialogs, the client-certificate passphrase and font fields are named;
  labels use sentence case; import and export summaries say nested collections
  rather than folders; dark-mode checkboxes, switches, dividers and chart legends
  are legible; and numbers, latencies and run kinds read the same on every
  screen (#2284, #2285, #2288, #2296, #2301, #2302, #2305, #2309, #2311, #2313,
  #2318).

### Security

- A script or a redirect can no longer send a request to Vayu's own engine or
  MCP port (#2355).
- Mock servers and the inbox take an `allowedOrigins` list per listener (#2367).
  A listener used to echo any `Origin` with credentials allowed, so any open web
  page could read the examples it served. It now sends no credentials, and the
  list restricts which origins may read it.
- The app's file-read channels read only files you picked (#2357). A file in a
  form-data part or a binary body is read from the file the check approved, so
  a link swapped in afterwards is not followed (#2416, #2678).
- `pm.cookies.jar()` reads only the request's own site (#2358).
- An OpenAPI `$ref` to a loopback or link-local address is refused, and no
  redirect is followed (#2364). A monitor on a link-local or cloud-metadata host
  needs an allowlist entry (#2370).
- Postman client certificates are registered only when you tick them (#2363).
- A script timeout of 0 and an oversized script stack are no longer accepted,
  and a script's thrown text is bounded in the log (#2359).
- A response, request body, data cell or JSON string field nested about 100,000
  levels used to crash the engine. It is now refused or read as not JSON
  (#2361, #2362, #2413, #2417, #2671, #2672).
